sections.title: Linear equations
facts: Name the unknown, write what the words say, then do the same to both sides.
Clear fractions first: multiply both sides by a common denominator.
"$5$ less than $x$" is $x - 5$; "$x$ less than $5$" is $5 - x$.
Consecutive numbers: $n$, $n + 1$, $n + 2$. Consecutive odd or even: $n$, $n + 2$, $n + 4$. The middle one is the average.
$ax + b = cx + d$ has no solution when $a = c$ but $b \neq d$, and every $x$ works when $a = c$ and $b = d$.

sections.title: Systems of equations
facts: Add or subtract the equations to cancel a letter; or solve one for a letter and substitute.
Sum $s$ and difference $d$: the numbers are $\frac{s + d}{2}$ and $\frac{s - d}{2}$.
Asked for $x + y$? Try adding the equations: $3x + 2y = 17$ and $2x + 3y = 13$ give $5(x + y) = 30$.
$x + y$, $y + z$ and $x + z$ add up to $2(x + y + z)$.
Parallel lines (same $x$ and $y$ ratio, different constant) have no common solution.

sections.title: Distance, rate & time
facts: $d = rt$. Match the units: $15$ minutes $= \frac{1}{4}$ hour.
Towards each other: speeds add. Chasing in the same direction: speeds subtract.
Downstream $=$ boat $+$ current; upstream $=$ boat $-$ current. The current is half the difference.
Average speed $=$ total distance $\div$ total time.

sections.title: Work & mixtures
facts: A job done in $t$ hours is done at $\frac{1}{t}$ per hour. Together, rates add; a drain's rate subtracts.
Two workers taking $a$ and $b$ hours together take $\frac{ab}{a + b}$ hours.
Worker-days: $w$ workers for $d$ days is $wd$ worker-days of work.
Mixtures: pure amount $=$ percent $\times$ total. Pure amounts add and totals add.
Adding water keeps the pure amount the same; adding pure stuff raises both the pure amount and the total.

sections.title: Ages, coins & money
facts: Ages: make a table with a column for each time. Everyone ages by the same number of years.
The difference between two people's ages never changes.
Coins: one equation for how MANY coins, one for how much they are WORTH. Work in cents.
Quick trick: pretend every coin is the cheaper kind, then each dearer coin adds the difference in value.
